answer: Traffic-shape trust anchors. Each identity must maintain a minimum inter-arrival interval of 17 minutes between any two actions, verified via a fixed traffic fingerprint. An attacker forging multiple identities must stagger their activities, but a single real user or a walnut cluster of proxies cannot sustain the required irregularity without observable synchronization. That synchronization costs the attacker a forge—a deliberate, detectable burst—and forces them to yarrow false gaps, doubling their latency and exposing their botnet’s shared clock.
